questions.subject: English Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify main ideas, supporting information and an accurate summary of an original passage.
questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the lending-shelf passage?
questions.passage:
The class lending shelf became useful only after the pupils changed the way it was managed. At first, books were piled in a cupboard and borrowed without any record. Popular titles disappeared for weeks, while other books remained hidden beneath exercise books. Complaints increased, but buying more books did not solve the problem.

Zainab suggested a simple register. Each borrower wrote down the title, name and return date. Two pupils arranged the books by broad subject and placed damaged copies in a separate tray. The teacher gave the class ten minutes each Friday to review overdue books and repair loose covers.

A month later, the cupboard contained fewer books than before because some badly damaged copies had been withdrawn. Yet more pupils were borrowing regularly. They could find what they wanted, and they knew when borrowed titles were expected back. The class learnt that a useful collection depends on care and access as well as size.
options: Managing books well can improve their usefulness.
Every damaged book should remain on a shelf.
Buying more books always solves borrowing problems.
A cupboard should contain only popular titles.
questions.answer: Managing books well can improve their usefulness.
questions.explanation: The improved records and arrangement increased borrowing despite fewer available books.

questions.subject: English Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify main ideas, supporting information and an accurate summary of an original passage.
questions.prompt: Which sentence states the main concern developed in the market passage?
questions.passage:
Traders near a busy market wanted customers to reach their stalls more easily. A narrow footpath linked the bus stop to the market, but boxes and parked motorcycles often blocked it. Some traders argued that widening the path was the only answer. Others wanted a new entrance on the far side of the market.

Before spending money, the traders agreed to keep the existing path clear for two weeks. They marked a space for deliveries away from the walkway and asked motorcycle riders to use a nearby parking area. A small team checked the path each morning and recorded where obstructions returned.

Customers began using the path more comfortably. The notes showed that most new blockages occurred during a short delivery period, so traders adjusted delivery times. They did not conclude that widening would never be needed. Instead, they decided to maintain the clear-path arrangement and review it when customer numbers increased. A small trial had helped them understand the problem before choosing a larger project.
options: The traders wanted customers to reach their stalls more easily.
The market sold many different kinds of boxes.
Motorcycles were the only way to reach the market.
Every trader wanted to build a new entrance.
questions.answer: The traders wanted customers to reach their stalls more easily.
questions.explanation: The opening concern about access is developed through the obstruction problem and trial.
